system_description.narrative_title: AI trade vs. Macro: Nvidia, CoreWeave and a rising-rate shock
system_description.narrative_summary: News converge on a single dynamic: sector-specific AI catalysts (Nvidia leadership turmoil, CoreWeave results, data‑centre build debates) are colliding with macro legacies — rising inflation, hawkish Fed expectations and a bond‑market repricing. As an open system, the AI investment boom takes flows, policy signals and corporate events as inputs and outputs asset‑price revaluations, financing stress for data‑centre and chip investments, and shifting investor risk allocation. Feedback loops (higher yields compress growth valuations → equity selloffs → tighter financing for AI buildouts → political/regulatory responses) create systemic sensitivity and contagion risk across markets.
system_description.scope: Interactions among AI sector companies and projects (chipmakers, cloud/data‑centre providers), equity and credit market pricing and flows, investor sentiment and concentration, monetary policy expectations and sovereign bond markets, and near‑term financing/capital‑allocation decisions.
system_description.super_system: Global financial and macroeconomic system (global capital markets, central banks, and real‑economy inflation dynamics).

variables.name: AI sector capital inflows
variables.description: The net monetary flow into AI‑related investment vehicles, projects and fundraising over a given period.

variables.name: AI market capitalization concentration
variables.description: The degree to which market capitalization and investment in the AI sector is concentrated among a small number of assets or issuers.

variables.name: Equity valuation multiples
variables.description: Average price‑to‑earnings/price‑to‑sales style valuation ratios across equities, especially growth/technology cohorts.

variables.name: Technology sector credit spreads
variables.description: The premium charged on debt issued to technology and infrastructure projects over risk‑free yields, reflecting perceived credit risk.

variables.name: Long‑term sovereign bond yield
variables.description: The prevailing yield on long‑duration sovereign debt instruments that anchors discount rates for long‑horizon assets.

variables.name: Policy rate expectations
variables.description: Market and agent expectations about the future path of central bank policy rates over the relevant horizon.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: The expected future rate of consumer‑price inflation over short and medium term horizons as perceived by markets and agents.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion
variables.description: The aggregate propensity of investors to shun risky assets in favor of safe assets, measured by risk premia and demand shifts.

variables.name: Corporate capital expenditure commitments
variables.description: The stock of announced and contracted capital spending plans for large technology and infrastructure projects awaiting execution.

variables.name: Project financing cost
variables.description: The effective cost of capital (debt and equity blended) for financing long‑lived technology and infrastructure projects.

variables.name: Market liquidity
variables.description: The ease and depth with which assets can be transacted without large price impact across equity and credit markets.

variables.name: Equity fund flow volatility
variables.description: The variability and frequency of net flows into and out of equity funds and ETFs that amplify price moves.

variables.name: Regulatory and political pressure
variables.description: The intensity of policy, regulatory or political scrutiny and potential intervention targeting sector activity or assets.

variables.name: Semiconductor production capacity
variables.description: The available fabrication and packaging capacity for advanced semiconductors relative to industry demand.

variables.name: Data‑center infrastructure capacity
variables.description: The available power, cooling and physical space capacity to host large‑scale data‑center operations.

variables.name: Financial linkage degree
variables.description: The extent of interconnected exposures and cross‑holdings between financial institutions, asset managers and sector counterparties.

catalysts.title: Fed rate‑hike decision pressure (mid‑Dec)
catalysts.description: Market expectations and Fed officials' comments point to a likely policy‑rate increase or clearer tightening path around the December meeting, moving yields and risk premia.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Broad Price Pressures Firm Up Case for Fed Rate Increase in December'; 'Fed Forced to Confront Case for Bigger and Faster Rate Rises'.

catalysts.title: Near‑term inflation and housing data releases
catalysts.description: Upcoming US (and global) inflation and housing prints will likely reprice rates and inflation expectations, affecting Treasury yields and risk assets.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. inflation is already bad enough. It might get worse.'; 'Treasury Yields Rise, European Bond Yields Fall'; 'await fresh inflation and housing data'.

catalysts.title: Continued Treasury auction weakness and bond selloff
catalysts.description: Ongoing weak demand at auctions and investor selling could push long yields higher and compress market liquidity, pressuring risk assets.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. 30‑Year Treasury Auction Shows Softer Demand'; 'Treasuries slide as “hot” inflation sparks bets on Fed rate rise'; 'Treasury Selloff Accelerates'.

catalysts.title: Ongoing Nvidia leadership crisis and scrutiny
catalysts.description: The CEO exit and governance concerns will likely continue to unsettle markets, trigger regulatory scrutiny, and reprice concentration and flows in the AI trade.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia CEO's exit rattles AI stocks'; 'Analysis: Nvidia’s leadership crisis tests the chipmaker’s role'; 'US senator wants assessment of whether Nvidia is too big to fail.'

catalysts.title: CoreWeave chip‑backed debt deal and expansion
catalysts.description: CoreWeave's planned multibillion dollar chip‑backed debt issuance and capex push could ease AI cloud financing constraints and revive related stocks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'CoreWeave plans multibillion‑dollar chip‑backed debt deal'; 'CoreWeave soars ... after strong Q3 report'; 'CoreWeave Finds a Workaround to Capital Constraints—for Now.'

catalysts.title: Political/regulatory pushback on data‑centre builds
catalysts.description: Threats and local/regional resistance to data‑centre build‑outs could slow capacity additions, raise costs and reroute AI capex plans.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AI jitters erupt after Democrats threaten data centre build‑out'; 'United Airlines bans AI agents'; 'Can green cement decarbonise the data centre building boom?'.
